BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City MAY 13 www.dilq.qov.ph s. 204±1 PILG OPINION NO Ar. RICHARD M. GARCIA National President United Architects of the Philippines Dear Ar. Garcia: This has reference to your letter dated 24 January 2024 seeking the Department's legal opinion and clarifications on the following matters: 1. The specific implications of the recent resolutions on the roles and responsibilities of Civil Engineers and Architects in the context of Building Permits Application and Approval; 2. Guidelines for local government units in interpreting and implementing resolutions to address potential conflicts or overlapping practices between Civil Engineering and Architecture; and 3. Recommendations for ensuring that the Building Permits process remains efficient, transparent, and compliant with the legal framework, considering the recent developments in the DPWH vs. PICE vs. UAP case. Your query is premised by the implications of the latest Supreme Court ruling on the case of Department of Public Works and Highways v. Philippine Institute of Civil Engineers, Inc. v. United Architects of the Philippines decided by the Supreme Court. Pursuant to your submission, the resolution of the case may have implications on the procedures and criteria for the issuance of Building Permits at the local level. It was mentioned that the uncertainty surrounding the delineation of responsibilities between civil engineers and architects in the design and construction process could potentially affect the efficiency and effectiveness of the Building Permit Application and Approval process. It was then emphasized that there remains a need for clarity on how local government units should interpret and implement these guidelines to ensure a standardized and consistent approach in the issuance of Building Permits. Thus, the request for guidance and clarification. As to the the Supreme Court in its recent ruling in the consolidated case of Department of Public Works and Highways v. Philippine Institute of Civil Engineers Inc., v. United Architects of the Philippinesl, provides that the copy of the National Building Code published in the Official Gazette should be considered as the controlling and official version. G.R. NOS. 200015 and 205846, dated 15 March 2023 "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.. 8876-34-54

Considering that the phrase "licensed architect or civil engineer in case of architectural and structural plans" was not included in the published version of the National Building Code, this proviso cannot be considered to have any legal effect nor part of the National Building Code. Thus, this Department will follow the ruling of the Supreme Court in the abovementioned case that only registered and licensed architects may prepare, sign, and seal the architectural documents listed in Section 302(4)(a), (c), (d), (e), and (f) of the Revised Implementing Rules, while only registered and licensed architects, or interior designers, may prepare, sign, and seal the architectural interior/interior design documents enumerated under Section 302(4)(b) of the same rules. Accordingly, it is ministerial for local government units to reject building permit applications that do not include the required signatures and certifications. Furthermore, without the relevant signatures required by the rules, the LGU may withhold approval or take enforcement action, such as issuing stop-work orders, against construction projects that proceed without the necessary approvals. As to the second query, it should be noted that this Department is an agency of the executive branch of government and, as such, lacks the authority to interpret laws and high court rulings. The department may only enforce the laws and the Supreme Court decisions to handle potential conflicts or overlapping practices regarding the application of building permits in LGUs. Following the principle of local autonomy which confines this Department's authority within the ambit of plain general supervision, the department is precluded to intervene with LGUs internal affairs. As such, LGUs determine what is best in implementing the general guidelines issued by the national government pertaining to the application of building permits in their respective jurisdictions. Said implementation should be without undue interference or dictation from the central government. The Executive Department may only check whether local governments or their officials were performing their duties as provided by fundamental laws and statutes. It cannot interfere with local governments, so long as they act within the scope of their authority.2 Therefore on the subject matter pertaining interpreting and implementing resolutions to address potential conflicts or overlapping practices between Civil Engineering and Architecture, the same may be beyond the supervisory authority of this Department. Perhaps, it may be best investigated by the Professional Regulations Commission (PRC) and/or other competent authorities. Be that as it may, as to the last query, what the department may consider is to recommend LGUs' to compliance with the decision of the Supreme Court in verifying the documents submitted to them before issuing the building permits. The Department may only recommend LGUs' familiarization with the subject decision in relation to Section 302 of the Revised Implementing Rules of the National Building Code. Nonetheless, the Bureau of Local Government Development (BLGD), this Department, is copy furnished for any policy amendment/formulation measures, taking into account the concerns submitted by your association. 2 Taule V. Santos, G.R. NO. 90336, 12 August 1991 Page 2 of 3

The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY THE AU HORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATTY N VICT R.
